new_assertions.body: In complete 5x3-k3, the tested T2-O scalar decoder has GF(2) polynomial degree at most two relative to exact-rank component-parity coordinates.
The 18 affine contradictions were evaluator-model insufficiency rather than evidence that the tested scalar Q needed another coordinate: changing D alone removes them.

The four-row rectangle certificates are exactly the second-discrete-derivative obstructions expected when a degree-1 model is missing pair interactions; their disappearance under degree two is structurally coherent with that diagnosis.
Finite polynomial degree is a separate optimization axis from Q coarseness. A smaller Q may require a higher-degree D, while a refined Q can linearize part of D.
The full degree-2 existence construction is radically underdetermined and therefore cannot be interpreted as a stable component-pair valuation without additional minimality or transfer evidence.
Cross-geometry transfer now dominates local fitting: 4x4-k4 is the required independent falsifier because it retains 168 exact-rank degree-1 contradictions under the same frozen producer.
